title: Region-aware tier & fallback observability playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a structured, storage-efficient observability playbook for smart routing decisions (region selection, tier routing, fallback model variants) to make per-request provenance, per-hop metrics, and decision rationale queryable for SLO debugging and RCA without exploding retention costs.
background: We currently capture routing decisions in coarse audit logs and occasional traces. Debugging cross-region fallbacks and tier routing regressions requires manual correlation of request logs, model metrics, and routing engine events. This work is driven by recent customer incidents where silent fallback to a lower-tier variant increased token latency and cost; operators lacked per-hop decision timing and rationale for root cause analysis.
goals: 1) Define a compact routing-decision envelope schema that records region, tier, variant, rationale tags, latency/cost deltas per hop. 2) Add sampling and adaptive retention policies to keep storage bounded. 3) Expose queryable fields in Console and Grafana for SLO correlation and live debugging. 4) Provide a migration plan to backfill high-priority incidents for retrospective analysis.
success_metrics: - Mean time to diagnose routing incidents reduced from 3.2h to <45m for routing-related SRE tickets. - Percentage of routing incidents with full per-hop telemetry available >= 90% for P1/P0 events. - Routing-telemetry ingestion growth <= 15% while retaining 6 months of critical envelopes.
acceptance_criteria: - Envelope schema reviewed and approved by infra + security. - End-to-end trace emitted for sample traffic including hop timings, rationale tags, model variant IDs. - Console search and Grafana dashboard surfaces region/tier/fallback breakdowns with links to request envelope. - Sampling controls available and documented; default policy configured. - PR merged and a canary rollout to 10% of production traffic with no observable latency regression (>99th percentile preserved).
design_proposal: We will introduce a compact 'route_envelope' protobuf with the following top-level fields: request_id, timestamp, route_hash, selected_region, selected_tier, variant_id, hop_list (serialized as delimited compact records), decision_reasons (list of tokens), latency_ns, token_cost_delta. To avoid large payloads, hop entries will include fixed-width fields and optional compressed ctx snapshots stored in an object store; envelopes keep pointers only. Sampling will be twofold: always-capture for P0/P1 errors and 1-in-N probabilistic capture for normal traffic (configurable by route and tenant). Envelopes will be indexed for route_hash, variant_id, and region. Retention tiering: 90 days for full envelopes for high-impact customers, 14 days for low-tier captures, 6 months for aggregated rollups only.
tradeoffs: - Compact binary schema reduces storage but requires migration tooling to read older envelopes. - Pointer-to-artifact approach keeps envelopes small but adds cross-store complexity and potential for missing artifacts if object-store retention mismatches. - Aggressive sampling reduces cost but can miss rare regressions; mitigated by on-error always-capture and dynamic sampling bumps based on anomaly detectors.
implementation_steps: 1) Define proto and serialization format; RFC review. 2) Implement envelope emission in routing decision service with async write path. 3) Add sampling controller with route-config and tenant overrides. 4) Index ingestion pipeline updates to populate Elasticsearch/Clickhouse views for Console queries. 5) Console UX: per-request envelope viewer and route-level aggregates. 6) Grafana dashboards and alerts for sudden increases in fallback rates by region/tier. 7) QA, canary rollout, and full rollout.

risks: - Object-store pointer model may fail for high-cardinality debug snapshots unless TTLs are carefully aligned. - Indexing many small envelopes could increase write amplification. - Risk of exposing internal rationale tokens in logs; must run through security review and PII scrubbing.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for proto roundtrip and sampling behavior. - Integration test sending simulated region-fallback traffic through canary and asserting envelope emission and indexability. - Chaos test: simulate region outage and confirm fallback envelopes captured and surfaced in Console. - Load test to verify ingestion pipeline handles expected QPS with sampling.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Canary (10% of traffic) for 48h to non-critical routes. Phase 2: 50% coverage with sampling at 1-in-100 and error-capture enabled for 7 days. Phase 3: Global default rollout with sampling policy tuned per-route. Provide rollback toggle per-cluster. Post-rollout: 2-week monitoring window and incident review.
